TreVeyon Henderson.status: Full practice Wednesday - ankle; trending toward Week 2 return
TreVeyon Henderson.note: Henderson progressed from limited work Monday to a full practice Wednesday as he returns from the ankle injury that kept him out of Week 1. The full session materially improves both Week 2 availability and workload confidence, though a small cushion remains until New England confirms his game status and intended role.
TreVeyon Henderson.expectedReturn: Week 2 increasingly likely; final game status pending

Zach Charbonnet.note: Unavailable for at least the first four games while rehabbing a torn ACL. Seattle has been encouraged by his rehab, but there is no firm return date.

Tory Horton.status: Full practice Wednesday - hamstring; Week 2 return likely
Tory Horton.note: Horton progressed from a Week 1 inactive and prior limited work to full participation Wednesday. The unrestricted session materially improves confidence that the hamstring will not keep him out of Week 2, while a small workload and recurrence cushion remains until final game status.
Tory Horton.expectedReturn: Week 2 likely; final game status pending

George Kittle.note: Successfully returned from the January Achilles tear in San Francisco's Week 1 win over the Rams, catching two of five targets for 12 yards with no reported in-game setback. His usage remained below a normal Kittle workload, but completing the game materially improves near-term availability confidence. Participation is expected to increase progressively in coming weeks.
George Kittle.expectedReturn: Active; workload expected to ramp up

Rome Odunze.status: Active Week 1 - calf; cleared through pregame testing
Rome Odunze.note: Odunze is officially active against Carolina after passing through pregame testing without a reported setback. That removes the remaining short-term availability uncertainty from his questionable designation. A modest workload cushion remains because he was limited in all three game-week practices while returning from the right calf strain.
Rome Odunze.expectedReturn: Active Week 1; modest workload limitation still possible

Jonathon Brooks.status: Cleared Week 1 - groin resolved; no limitations
Jonathon Brooks.note: Carolina removed Brooks from the final Week 1 injury report after he practiced fully Friday. Head coach Dave Canales said Brooks has no limitations entering the opener. The groin-related availability and workload penalties are removed; the residual long-term-risk modifier reflects his history of back-to-back right ACL surgeries rather than the resolved groin issue.

Zay Flowers.status: DNP Wednesday - aggravated left hamstring; Week 2 uncertain
Zay Flowers.note: Flowers did not practice Wednesday as Baltimore opened Week 2 preparation after he aggravated the same hamstring issue that affected him in preseason. The injury is still described as day-to-day and not believed serious, but the first official practice absence materially lowers confidence in a Week 2 return and modestly increases recurrence/workload risk until he resumes practice.

Michael Penix Jr..status: Inactive Week 1 - ACL return; targeting Week 2-3
Michael Penix Jr..note: Penix remains out for the opener while Atlanta completes his return-to-game ramp from the 2025 ACL tear, but Ian Rapoport now reports that he is specifically targeting Week 2 or Week 3 for his 2026 debut. That materially tightens and improves the prior open-ended timeline, so near-term availability is raised while the workload and residual post-ACL risk modifiers remain unchanged.

Tua Tagovailoa.note: Atlanta has ruled Tagovailoa out for the Week 1 opener after the oblique injury suffered during Thursday practice. He was absent from the media-access portion of Friday practice, and Cooper Rush will start against Pittsburgh. No firm return timetable beyond Week 1 has been announced, so Week 2 remains possible but uncertain.

Alvin Kamara.status: Full practice Wednesday - MCL; Week 2 return likely
Alvin Kamara.note: Kamara was a full participant Wednesday, and head coach Kellen Moore said he feels good about Kamara's chances of playing against Baltimore. The full session is a material improvement from the prior Week 2 target without practice confirmation, sharply improving near-term availability and workload confidence while retaining a small MCL recurrence cushion.
Alvin Kamara.expectedReturn: Week 2 likely; final game status pending

Isiah Pacheco.note: Dan Campbell confirmed Monday that Pacheco required surgery for the back injury, and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports the procedure removed a body pressing on a nerve. The reported recovery timeline is approximately 12 weeks, with a chance to return in early December. That is materially worse than the prior open-ended Week 5-or-later outlook and warrants a substantial near-term availability downgrade plus added return-to-workload and residual back-risk penalties.

Tank Dell.note: On injured reserve with a knee issue and unavailable until at least Week 5.

James Conner.note: On injured reserve with a foot injury and unavailable for the opening portion of the season.

Jeremiyah Love.status: Active Week 1 - high ankle sprain; reduced workload possible
Jeremiyah Love.note: Arizona officially made Love active against the Chargers, confirming his NFL debut after he returned to practice only last week following the high-ankle sprain. The prior final availability uncertainty is removed, but the workload penalty remains because of the recent injury and expected backfield split.

Josh Jacobs.note: Currently unavailable to play because of an off-field league status with no established football return date. This adjustment reflects availability uncertainty, not injury performance risk.

Brock Bowers.status: DNP Wednesday - meniscus trim; Week 2 return uphill
Brock Bowers.note: Bowers did not practice Wednesday and has yet to take practice reps since the meniscus trim that kept him out of Week 1. Las Vegas still considers him day-to-day and hopes he can practice Thursday or Friday, but the Wednesday DNP makes a Week 2 return less likely and supports a modest workload restriction if he is cleared.
Brock Bowers.expectedReturn: Week 2 still possible but increasingly uncertain; Week 3-4 remains plausible

Malik Nabers.note: Nabers is officially active for Sunday Night Football against Dallas after practicing fully throughout the week. That resolves the prior game-time availability uncertainty and materially improves his near-term outlook. A modest workload cushion remains because this is his first regular-season game back from ACL reconstruction with meniscus repair and a later follow-up procedure, and the Giants have not ruled out managing his snaps.
Malik Nabers.expectedReturn: Active Week 1; modest workload management still possible

Xavier Legette.note: Not listed on Carolina's Week 1 injury report after recovering from the August ankle injury and walking-boot period. He is medically cleared for the opener; any playing-time limitation is role-based rather than injury-based.

Jakobi Meyers.note: Jacksonville gave Meyers no final game designation after three limited practices with the thumb injury. He is cleared to play against Cleveland. A very small workload cushion remains because he practiced in a non-contact jersey earlier in the week and the injury involves his catching hand, but the prior availability concern is removed.

Marvin Mims Jr..status: Estimated DNP Wednesday - foot; Week 2 status uncertain
Marvin Mims Jr..note: Denver's Wednesday report was an estimation because the team did not practice after playing Monday night, but Mims was listed as a non-participant with a foot injury. That is a meaningful reversal from the prior expectation that he would be fine for Week 2 after returning to Monday's game. Thursday-Friday participation will determine whether the downgrade persists.
Marvin Mims Jr..expectedReturn: Week 2 uncertain; Thursday-Friday practice participation pending

Patrick Mahomes.note: Fully cleared following ACL/LCL rehabilitation and expected to start Week 1. Mahomes has reported no planned playing restrictions; only a minimal residual long-term post-reconstruction risk modifier remains until regular-season game action is confirmed.

A.J. Brown.status: IR - high-ankle sprain; approximately six-week absence expected
A.J. Brown.note: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport now reports Brown is expected to miss about six weeks with the right high-ankle sprain, a more specific and slightly longer outlook than the prior four-to-six-week range. New England has already placed him on injured reserve. The tighter six-week expectation lowers near-term availability and adds a modest return-to-workload and reinjury cushion.
A.J. Brown.expectedReturn: Approximately six weeks; likely Week 7-8 range

Sam Darnold.status: Expected OUT multiple weeks - glute soft-tissue injury; about four-week return-to-play timeline
Sam Darnold.note: NFL Network's Mike Garafolo now reports Darnold is looking at about a four-week return-to-play timeline for the glute injury, with a chance to return somewhat sooner. This is materially more specific and less optimistic than the prior Week 3-4 possibility. Seattle still considers the injury short-term and has not placed him on injured reserve, but the clearer multi-week expectation warrants lower near-term availability plus modest workload and recurrence cushions for his eventual return.
Sam Darnold.expectedReturn: About four weeks from Week 1 injury; early October possible, potentially sooner

Alec Pierce.status: Active Week 1 - heel/ankle surgery recovery; 20-30 snap count expected
Alec Pierce.note: NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports Pierce is expected to play only about 20 to 30 snaps against Baltimore in Week 1. That is materially more restrictive than the prior generic managed-workload expectation and confirms a sharply reduced opening-week role while he completes his return from offseason lower-leg surgery. Availability remains full because he is expected to be active; the workload multiplier is reduced to reflect the concrete snap cap.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt.note: Washington says its full 53-man roster is medically cleared for Week 1, including Croskey-Merritt after he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the groin injury. A modest workload cushion remains because the team indicated snap-count decisions could still be discussed for players returning from injuries, but he no longer carries a meaningful availability penalty.

De'Zhaun Stribling.status: IR - ankle surgery for ruptured deltoid ligament; close to 10 weeks expected
De'Zhaun Stribling.note: Kyle Shanahan confirmed Stribling underwent surgery to repair a ruptured deltoid ligament in his left ankle and is expected to miss close to 10 weeks. This is materially worse than the prior one-month-plus estimate when surgery was only being considered, warranting a major near-term availability downgrade and additional return-to-workload and residual-risk penalties.

Sean Tucker.status: Full practice Wednesday - hamstring; Week 2 return likely
Sean Tucker.note: Tucker logged a full Wednesday practice after missing Week 1 with the hamstring injury. The unrestricted session materially improves his Week 2 availability and workload outlook, leaving only a minimal short-term soft-tissue recurrence cushion.
Sean Tucker.expectedReturn: Week 2 likely; final game status pending

Jalen McMillan.status: Full practice Wednesday - knee; Week 2 return likely
Jalen McMillan.note: McMillan practiced fully Wednesday after missing Week 1 because of the knee issue. The unrestricted session is a meaningful improvement from last week's doubtful/inactive status and makes a Week 2 return likely, with only a small residual workload and knee-risk cushion until final game status.
Jalen McMillan.expectedReturn: Week 2 likely; final game status pending

Dylan Sampson.status: IR - left knee; minimum four-game absence
Dylan Sampson.note: Cleveland officially placed Sampson on injured reserve September 15 after the left-knee injury suffered in Week 1. The transaction guarantees a minimum four-game absence and confirms the prior expectation that he would miss significant time. Availability is reduced modestly from the prior IR-possible assumption; return-to-workload and residual-risk multipliers remain unchanged until a more specific diagnosis or rehabilitation timeline is reported.
Dylan Sampson.expectedReturn: Eligible after four games; potentially before Cleveland's Oct. 18 game vs. Baltimore

Omar Cooper Jr..status: High-ankle sprain - week-to-week; expected to miss time
Omar Cooper Jr..note: Fresh Tuesday reporting says Cooper is now considered week-to-week with the ankle sprain and is expected to miss time, though the Jets are not placing him on injured reserve and are hopeful he can return within four weeks. That materially firms up the prior open-ended timeline and makes a Week 2 absence substantially more likely, so near-term availability is reduced while workload and long-term-risk multipliers remain unchanged.
Omar Cooper Jr..expectedReturn: Week-to-week; Jets hopeful for return within four weeks

Ja'Kobi Lane.status: IR - wrist surgery; minimum four-game absence
Ja'Kobi Lane.note: Baltimore officially placed Lane on injured reserve after wrist surgery, guaranteeing at least four missed games. The operation was already expected, but the IR transaction removes any chance of an earlier return and slightly lowers near-term availability while preserving the existing workload and residual-risk assumptions.
Ja'Kobi Lane.expectedReturn: Eligible after four games; recovery expected roughly four-to-six weeks

Kyler Murray.status: Limited Wednesday - concussion protocol; Week 2 chance improving
Kyler Murray.note: Murray progressed enough through the concussion protocol to participate on a limited basis Wednesday after earlier reporting made a Week 2 return unlikely. He still must complete the protocol and receive independent neurological clearance, but practicing is a meaningful improvement in near-term availability without changing expected workload once cleared.
Kyler Murray.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible pending concussion-protocol clearance; Week 3 if not cleared

Najee Harris.status: Healthy scratch Week 1 - Achilles medically cleared
Najee Harris.note: Updated reporting clarifies that Harris was not inactive because of the Achilles injury. He was a healthy scratch/coach's decision and was not listed on the Giants' injury report. The prior near-term availability and workload penalties are therefore removed. A small long-term-risk cushion remains because he is returning this season from the 2025 Achilles tear, but any Week 2 playing-time uncertainty is now treated as a depth-chart/role issue rather than an injury limitation.
Najee Harris.expectedReturn: Medically available Week 2; role/activation is coach's decision

Ladd McConkey.status: DNP Wednesday - rib injury; Week 2 availability unsettled
Ladd McConkey.note: McConkey did not practice Wednesday because of the rib injury suffered in Week 1. Earlier reporting described him as day-to-day and did not indicate a major injury, but missing the first formal Week 2 practice increases the chance of a Sunday absence and warrants a modest near-term availability and workload downgrade until Thursday-Friday participation is known.
Ladd McConkey.expectedReturn: Week 2 uncertain; Thursday-Friday practice progression pending

Chig Okonkwo.status: DNP Wednesday - hamstring; Week 2 availability in doubt
Chig Okonkwo.note: Okonkwo did not practice Wednesday after exiting Week 1 with a hamstring injury. Dan Quinn acknowledged uncertainty for the weekend. The confirmed first-practice absence materially lowers Week 2 availability and modestly increases workload and recurrence risk versus the prior status that was awaiting Wednesday participation.
Chig Okonkwo.expectedReturn: Week 2 in doubt; Thursday-Friday participation critical

Brian Thomas Jr..status: Expected active Week 2 - recurrent shoulder; limited practice planned
Brian Thomas Jr..note: Thomas briefly exited Jacksonville's Week 1 win after aggravating the same shoulder that bothered him late in preseason, then returned to the game. Head coach Liam Coen said Monday that Thomas will be limited in practice this week to reduce contact but that he fully expects him to play at Denver with no availability issue. The recurrence warrants a small workload and reinjury-risk cushion even though a missed game is not currently expected.
Brian Thomas Jr..expectedReturn: Expected active Week 2; limited practice/contact management this week

Nico Collins.status: Limited Wednesday - hamstring; Week 2 status requires monitoring
Nico Collins.note: Collins appeared on Houston's Wednesday injury report as a limited participant with a hamstring issue. He played through Week 1 and there is no confirmed multi-week absence, but a new soft-tissue injury for a high-value fantasy receiver warrants a modest availability, workload and recurrence-risk cushion until Thursday-Friday participation clarifies his status.
Nico Collins.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible; Thursday-Friday practice progression pending

RJ Harvey.status: Estimated DNP Wednesday - hamstring; Week 2 uncertain
RJ Harvey.note: Harvey appeared on Denver's Wednesday estimated injury report with a new hamstring issue and would not have practiced had the Broncos held a session. The team is on a short week after playing Monday night, so the new soft-tissue injury creates meaningful Week 2 availability and workload uncertainty until actual Thursday-Friday practice participation is known.
RJ Harvey.expectedReturn: Week 2 uncertain; Thursday-Friday practice participation pending

Jordan Mason.status: IR - fractured right thumb repaired; minimum four-game absence
Jordan Mason.note: Minnesota placed Mason on injured reserve Wednesday after a small fracture in his right thumb was repaired. He must miss at least four games, and Kevin O'Connell expressed optimism that Mason can return after the minimum absence. With Minnesota's Week 6 bye, Week 7 is his earliest game back. The hand injury also warrants a modest return-to-workload cushion for ball security and contact when activated.
Jordan Mason.expectedReturn: Week 7 earliest; expected back after minimum IR absence if healing stays on track

D'Andre Swift.status: Limited Wednesday - ankle/knee; Week 2 still expected
D'Andre Swift.note: Swift appeared on Chicago's Week 2 injury report with ankle and knee issues and was limited Wednesday. Current reporting indicates the issues are not believed serious and he is still expected to play, but the new dual lower-body designations justify a small near-term availability and workload cushion until he progresses later in the week.
D'Andre Swift.expectedReturn: Week 2 expected; Thursday-Friday practice progression pending
